headline_marked: Keychron's [[Thunderbolt 5 dock]] offers 80Gbps speeds and 140W charging
headline: Keychron's Thunderbolt 5 dock offers 80Gbps speeds and 140W charging
summary: The metal-clad dock boasts dual 8K monitor support and a wide array of ports, but requires the latest hardware to unlock its full potential.
details: Keychron, known for its keyboards, has launched a Thunderbolt 5 14-in-1 Docking Station. It features a robust metal construction with an industrial design, mirroring the aesthetics of their popular keyboards.
The dock supports 80Gbps bidirectional data speeds, an 80Gbps boost mode, and can drive dual monitors at 8K 60Hz or 4K 240Hz. It also offers up to 140W charging for compatible devices.
Connectivity includes three Thunderbolt 5 ports, microSD and SD card slots, a 2.5Gbps Ethernet port, four USB-A ports, and one USB-C port. A 3.5mm headphone jack is also present.
To fully utilize Thunderbolt 5's capabilities, users need a computer with a Thunderbolt 5 port. Older Thunderbolt 4 or earlier ports will not benefit from the increased speeds and features.

While the dock offers impressive specs, its utility can be limited by the user's existing hardware and setup. For instance, compatibility with certain Mac configurations for dual-monitor setups might be an issue.

Despite being potentially overkill for some, the dock proved useful for tasks like high-speed SSD backups, connecting microphones, and serving as a reliable card reader, demonstrating its versatility beyond peak performance.
The unit does get warm during operation, especially when placed horizontally. Users should also consider its modest desk footprint and the size of its power brick when planning its placement.

headline_marked: [[Ellis AI]] emerges from stealth with $10M for private credit managers
headline: Ellis AI emerges from stealth with $10M for private credit managers
summary: The new startup, founded by Cadre co-creator Ryan Williams, aims to streamline fragmented workflows for private credit managers using AI agents.
details: Ellis AI announced its emergence from stealth with $10 million in seed funding from prominent investors including First Round Capital, 645 Ventures, and Mellody Hobson.
The company, founded by Ryan Williams (co-creator of the real estate platform Cadre), aims to address the fragmented operational infrastructure in private markets.
Ellis uses AI agents to manage documents, spreadsheets, and correspondence, connecting and centralizing scattered software and accounting information for private credit firms.
The platform can flag data discrepancies and assist with tasks like portfolio monitoring and report preparation, potentially automating month-end closing processes.
Williams emphasizes that Ellis connects to existing systems rather than forcing a complete overhaul, keeping human experts in the loop for material decisions.
He believes the human role will narrow but not disappear, stating the goal is to augment human judgment, not replace it, enabling faster, educated decisions.
caption:
Repeat founder Ryan Williams has raised $10 million for Ellis AI, a new startup targeting private credit managers with AI agents.

Ellis AI announced its emergence from stealth with $10 million in seed funding from prominent investors including First Round Capital, 645 Ventures, and Mellody Hobson.

The company, founded by Ryan Williams (co-creator of the real estate platform Cadre), aims to address the fragmented operational infrastructure in private markets.

Ellis uses AI agents to manage documents, spreadsheets, and correspondence, connecting and centralizing scattered software and accounting information for private credit firms.

The platform can flag data discrepancies and assist with tasks like portfolio monitoring and report preparation, potentially automating month-end closing processes.

Williams emphasizes that Ellis connects to existing systems rather than forcing a complete overhaul, keeping human experts in the loop for material decisions.

He believes the human role will narrow but not disappear, stating the goal is to augment human judgment, not replace it, enabling faster, educated decisions.

Source: TechCrunch, DEV
